subject: English Language & Literature
basis: BCS_English_Final: Lecture 03 (Correction on Subject-Verb Agreement), Lecture 17 (Correction on Miscellaneous Common Mistakes)

o: I have been waiting here for two hours.
I have been waiting here since two hours.
I am waiting here since two hours.
I was waiting here since two hours.
questions.e: সময়ের পরিমাণে for; শুরুর বিন্দুতে since।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: He returned back home late at night.
He returned home late at night.
He returned back to home late at night.
He returned to back home late at night.
questions.e: return মানেই ফিরে আসা — back অপ্রয়োজনীয় (redundancy)।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: The reason for his absence is due to he is ill.
The reason for his absence is because he is ill.
The reason for his absence is that he is ill.
The reason for his absence because he is ill.
questions.e: the reason is that …; because-এর সঙ্গে reason দ্বিরুক্তি।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: Despite of rain, they went out.
Despite of the rain, they went out.
In spite the rain, they went out.
Despite the rain, they went out.
questions.e: despite (of ছাড়া) = in spite of।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: He is taller than his brother.
He is more taller than his brother.
He is most taller than his brother.
He is more tall than his brother.
questions.e: double comparative (more taller) ভুল।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: I am knowing him very well.
I know him very well.
I am knowing him very good.
I have knowing him very well.
questions.e: know, like, believe প্রভৃতি stative verb সাধারণত continuous-এ বসে না।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: Unless you will work hard, you will fail.
Unless you do not work hard, you will fail.
Unless you work hard, you will fail.
Unless you don't work hard, you will not fail.
questions.e: unless নিজেই নেতিবাচক — সঙ্গে not বসে না।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: Scarcely had he left then the guests arrived.
Scarcely had he left than the guests arrived.
Scarcely he had left when the guests arrived.
Scarcely had he left when the guests arrived.
questions.e: Scarcely/Hardly … when; No sooner … than।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: No sooner did he see me than he ran away.
No sooner did he see me when he ran away.
No sooner he saw me than he ran away.
No sooner did he saw me than he ran away.
questions.e: No sooner + inversion … than।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: He is enough strong to lift the box.
He is strong enough to lift the box.
He is strong enough for lift the box.
He is enough strong for lifting the box.
questions.e: adjective + enough (enough adjective-এর পরে বসে)।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)
questions.dup: Semantic Duplicate — ১৮-১৭ (old enough / enough old): একই নিয়ম

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: I prefer tea from coffee.
I prefer tea than coffee.
I prefer tea to coffee.
I prefer tea over than coffee.
questions.e: prefer A to B।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)
questions.dup: Semantic Duplicate — ২৮-৩০ (prefer donating money to distributing clothes): prefer … to নিয়ম

o: Let him to go.
Let he go.
Let his go.
Let him go.
questions.e: let-এর পরে objective case + bare infinitive।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)
questions.dup: Semantic Duplicate — ১২-২৩ (Let you and him be witnesses): let-এর পরে objective case

o: Supposing he comes, what will you do?
Supposing if he comes, what will you do?
Supposing he will come, what you will do?
Supposing if he come, what will you do?
questions.e: supposing নিজেই শর্ত বোঝায় — if অপ্রয়োজনীয়।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: Although he is poor, but he is honest.
Although he is poor, he is honest.
Although he is poor, yet but he is honest.
Though he is poor, but he is honest.
questions.e: although/though-এর সঙ্গে but বসে না (yet বসতে পারে)।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: He fluently speaks English language very.
He speaks fluently English.
He speaks English fluently.
He speaks English fluent.
questions.e: verb ও object-এর মাঝে adverb বসে না।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: He avoided meet me.
He avoided to meet me.
He avoided to meeting me.
He avoided meeting me.
questions.e: avoid-এর পরে gerund।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: My hair is turning grey.
My hairs are turning grey.
My hairs is turning grey.
My hair are turning grey.
questions.e: মাথার চুল সমষ্টিগতভাবে hair (uncountable) — singular verb।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: One must do his duty.
One must do one's duty.
One must do their duty.
One must do your duty.
questions.e: one-এর possessive one's।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)
questions.dup: Semantic Duplicate — ২৩-৯১ (One should be careful about one's duty): একই নিয়ম

o: He said me that he would come.
He told that he would come.
He said that he would come.
He told to me that he would come.
questions.e: tell-এর পরে ব্যক্তিবাচক object লাগে; object ছাড়া said that।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: She explained me about the problem.
She explained me the problem.
She explained to me about the problem.
She explained the problem to me.
questions.e: explain something to someone।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: We reached the station at noon.
We reached at the station at noon.
We reached to the station at noon.
We reached on the station at noon.
questions.e: reach-এর পরে preposition বসে না।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: The cost of these books are high.
The cost of these books is high.
The cost of these book are high.
The costs of these books is high.
questions.e: মূল subject cost (singular) — verb is।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: The poor man was dead last night.
The poor man was died last night.
The poor man died last night.
The poor man has died last night.
questions.e: die intransitive — was died হয় না; last night → past simple।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: This is the girl whom I think she is honest.
This is the girl whom I think is honest.
This is the girl which I think is honest.
This is the girl who I think is honest.
questions.e: I think মধ্যবর্তী বাক্যাংশ; who হলো is-এর subject — whom নয়।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: I have a lot of work to do.
I have a lot of works to do.
I have many works to do.
I have a lot of work to doing.
questions.e: কাজ অর্থে work uncountable; works = সাহিত্যকর্ম/কারখানা।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: He bought two dozens eggs.
He bought two dozen eggs.
He bought two dozens of egg.
He bought two dozen egg.
questions.e: সংখ্যার পরে dozen, hundred ইত্যাদিতে s বসে না।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: He is a five-years old boy.
He is a five-years-old boy.
He is a five-year-old boy.
He is a five year olds boy.
questions.e: compound adjective-এ noun singular থাকে।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: The two brothers quarrelled with themselves.
The two brothers quarrelled with one another.
The two brothers quarrelled each other.
The two brothers quarrelled with each other.
questions.e: দুজনের মধ্যে each other; দুইয়ের বেশি হলে one another।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: The book has been lying on the table since morning.
The book is lying on the table since morning.
The book lies on the table since morning.
The book was lying on the table since morning.
questions.e: since-যুক্ত চলমান কাজ — present perfect continuous।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: Of the two sisters, Rina is the best singer.
Of the two sisters, Rina is the better singer.
Of the two sisters, Rina is best singer.
Of the two sisters, Rina is a most good singer.
questions.e: দুজনের তুলনায় comparative (better)।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: He hardly works hard to support his family.
He works hardly to support his family.
He works hard to support his family.
He works hardly for support his family.
questions.e: hard = কঠোরভাবে; hardly = কদাচিৎ।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: She sings beautifulness.
She sings beautiful.
She beautiful sings.
She sings beautifully.
questions.e: verb-কে বিশেষিত করতে adverb (beautifully)।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

questions.q: Identify the incorrect part of the sentence: 'He has (A) returned (B) the book (C) yesterday (D).'
o: (A) has
(B) returned
(C) the book
(D) yesterday
questions.e: yesterday (নির্দিষ্ট অতীত) থাকলে present perfect নয় — returned।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)
questions.dup: Semantic Duplicate — ৩৬-৬৩ (Yesterday, he went home): yesterday-র সঙ্গে past simple

o: He is a man of little words.
He is a man of few words.
He is a man of less words.
He is a man of a little words.
questions.e: গণনাযোগ্য noun (words)-এর সঙ্গে few; little অগণনীয় noun-এর সঙ্গে।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: He is my cousin-brother of mine.
He is my cousin brother.
He is my cousin.
He is cousin brother to me.
questions.e: ইংরেজিতে cousin-ই যথেষ্ট; cousin brother/sister বাংলার আক্ষরিক অনুবাদজনিত ভুল।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: Rahim is elder to his sister.
Rahim is elder than his sister.
Rahim is more elder than his sister.
Rahim is older than his sister.
questions.e: elder শুধু attributive (my elder brother); than-এর সঙ্গে older।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: There are fewer students in the class today.
There are less students in the class today.
There is fewer students in the class today.
There are lesser students in the class today.
questions.e: গণনাযোগ্য (students) noun-এ fewer; অগণনীয় noun-এ less।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

o: He is both a singer as well as a dancer.
He is both a singer and a dancer.
He is both a singer or a dancer.
He is both a singer but a dancer.
questions.e: both-এর জোড়া and; as well as নয়।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: We must learn to cope up difficulties.
We must learn to cope up with difficulties.
We must learn to cope with difficulties.
We must learn to cope to difficulties.
questions.e: cope with (up নয়)।
questions.src: Lecture 03, 17 ও Standard Grammar Reference (Swan — Practical English Usage; Wren & Martin)
